```{r badges, include = FALSE}
# badges computed from DESCRIPTION, so that they never go stale
desc  <- read.dcf(file = "DESCRIPTION", fields = c("Version", "Depends", "License"))
r_min <- sub(pattern = ".*R \\(>= *([0-9.]+)\\).*", replacement = "\\1", x = desc[, "Depends"])
enc   <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub(pattern = "-", replacement = "--", x = x, fixed = TRUE)
  for (p in list(
      c(" ", "%20")
    , c("(", "%28")
    , c(")", "%29")
    , c(">", "%3E")
    , c("=", "%3D")
    , c("+", "%2B")
    , c("|", "%7C")
    )) {
    x <- gsub(pattern = p[1L], replacement = p[2L], x = x, fixed = TRUE)
  }
  x
}
lic   <- sub(pattern = " \\+ file LICENSE$", replacement = "", x = desc[, "License"])
lic_url <- if (grepl(pattern = "^MIT", x = lic)) "https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT" else if (grepl(
    pattern = "|"
  , x       = lic
  , fixed   = TRUE
  ))
  "https://www.gnu.org/licenses/licenses.html" else if (grepl(pattern = "GPL-3", x = lic))
  "https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html" else "https://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/gpl-2.0.html"
```

## Overview

**VetResearchLMM** gives the data sets and every analysis of Duchateau, Janssen and Rowlands (1998), *Linear Mixed
Models. An Introduction with Applications in Veterinary Research* (ILRI, Nairobi), with its own engine for linear
mixed models that gives the results the book prints from SAS PROC MIXED and PROC GLM.

* `vlm_fit()`: REML, ML or Type 3 (moment) estimation; random variance components, random coefficients
  (`vlm_random()`, VC or UN) and residual structures (`vlm_repeated()`: CS, AR(1), SP(POW), UN); the fixed-effects
  solution in the overparameterised coding; Type 3 or Type 1 tests with containment, residual, between-within,
  Satterthwaite or Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom; fit statistics;
* `vlm_lsmeans()`, `vlm_estimate()`, `vlm_contrast()`: least-squares means with Tukey, Bonferroni or Sidak
  comparisons, estimates in the broad and narrow inference spaces, and F tests of contrasts;
* `vlm_blup()`: best linear unbiased predictions of random effects;
* `vlm_ems()`: the analysis of variance with expected mean squares and synthesised F tests;
* `vlm_compare()`: information criteria and likelihood ratio tests of covariance structures;
* `vlm_interpret()`, `vlm_cite()`, `vlm_app()`: plain-language interpretation, references and a shiny application
  in which every example of the book loads with one click.

The help pages `?Examp1.3.2` to `?Examp3.3` give the SAS program of each example with the same analysis in R. The
package reproduces 115 of the 116 numbers of the book that it checks; the other one is printed truncated (3.685
for 3.6855). Version 2.0.0 keeps the data sets, the help topics and `emmeans_mixed_model()` and
`report_mixed_model()` of version 1.1.0, adds the data sets of Examples 1.2.2, 1.2.3 and 1.2.6, and corrects three
typing errors in `ex33`.

## Installation

```r
install.packages("VetResearchLMM")
# development version
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("myaseen208/VetResearchLMM")
```

## Quick start

The split-plot experiment of Example 1.2.5 (drugs given to herds within regions, doses to animals within herds):

```{r quick}
library(VetResearchLMM)
fm <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Pcv ~ Drug + dose + Drug:dose
    , data     = ex125
    , random   = ~ Region + Region:Drug
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = c("REML", "ML", "Type3")
    , ddfm     = "satterth"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
fm
vlm_interpret(
    x     = fm
  , alpha = 0.05
  , top   = 3L
  )
```

```{r quick-plot, fig.height = 4}
lm1 <-
  vlm_lsmeans(
      fit    = fm
    , specs  = ~ Drug:dose
    , at     = NULL
    , diff   = TRUE
    , adjust = "tukey"
    , level  = 0.95
    )
plot(x = lm1)
```

## Learn more

* Vignettes: `browseVignettes("VetResearchLMM")`, starting with `VetResearchLMM_01_getting_started`; PDF versions
  on the site.
* Site: <https://myaseen208.com/VetResearchLMM/>
* Notation: `vlm_notation()`
* References of the methods behind a result: `vlm_cite()`

## Citation

```{r citation, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
print(citation(package = "VetResearchLMM")[1L], style = "text")
```

BibTeX:

```{r citation-bib, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
print(citation(package = "VetResearchLMM")[1L], style = "bibtex")
```

Please also cite the book: `citation("VetResearchLMM")` lists it with the package, and `vlm_cite(x)` gives the
references of a single result.
